How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (6)

  1. In what year was ServiceNow founded?
    Company age is one input to maturity and viability.
  2. Which shareholders hold 5% or more of ServiceNow's voting stock, and in which countries are they based?
    Large or controlling shareholders affect ownership and country risk.
  3. Has ServiceNow made any workforce reductions in the last 24 months, and did they affect AI agent engineering or support teams?
    Workforce reductions can affect product support and roadmap.
  4. Have any financial-services customers ended or materially reduced their use of ServiceNow AI Agents in the last two years, and why?
    Loss of large customers can indicate product or service problems.
  5. Have any ServiceNow executives or directors left or been disciplined in connection with the matters under Department of Justice investigation or any other conduct issue?
    Leadership conduct issues can create reputational exposure.
  6. How are ServiceNow AI Agents licensed and priced, including any consumption units and the cost of Super Intelligence Control Tower?

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-12 · launch ServiceNow
    ServiceNow introduces Autonomous CRM Engine in controlled availability

    ServiceNow announced on 2026-11-12 Autonomous CRM Engine, a tool that maps how a customer's existing CRM is used, designs a target configuration and deploys approved changes into ServiceNow. The press release says the product is in controlled availability, with expanded capabilities expected in 2027. ServiceNow (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-11-10 · launch ServiceNow
    ServiceNow announces agentic continuous control monitoring for Integrated Risk Management

    ServiceNow announced on 2026-11-10 agentic capabilities for continuous control monitoring in its Integrated Risk Management product, extending monitoring to cloud, identity, SaaS and on-premises tools through more than 100 pre-built integrations. The press release says the monitoring works alongside the company's Super Intelligence Control Tower and that general availability is expected in the first quarter of 2027. ServiceNow (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  3. 2026-11-04 · layoff ServiceNow
    ServiceNow reported to have cut more staff in the UK, US and India; number not disclosed

    Reported by NowBen on 2026-11-05 and by CTech on 2026-11-06: ServiceNow carried out a further round of layoffs affecting employees in the UK, the US and India, which NowBen described as the third round of 2026 and said many employees learned of on 4 November. Neither outlet gives a number and ServiceNow has not disclosed one. Both quote a company statement that it is making "necessary changes to how we are structured" and is managing headcount to end 2026 where it started. CTech adds that ServiceNow's quarterly filing shows US$167 million of severance costs in the first nine months of 2026, and that its shares fell about 27% the day after third-quarter results. NowBen (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)CTech by Calcalist (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  4. 2026-06-05 · security incident ServiceNow
    ServiceNow discloses unauthorised queries of some customer instances

    Reported by BleepingComputer on 2026-06-09 and The Hacker News on 2026-06-10: ServiceNow told customers that a flaw allowing unauthenticated access to an API endpoint had been used to query tables in a subset of customer instances, mainly on the Australia release, and that it applied a fix to hosted instances on 2026-06-05. BleepingComputer reported that a later ServiceNow advisory attributed the activity to likely security research linked to bug bounty submissions. Neither article reported AI agent involvement. BleepingComputer (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)The Hacker News (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

    ServiceNow expands AI Control Tower to AI assets outside its own platform

    The Register reported on 2026-05-05 that ServiceNow had expanded AI Control Tower into five areas (discovery, observation, governance, security and measurement), with 30 new connectors to AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, SAP, Oracle and Workday, runtime tracing from its March 2026 purchase of Traceloop and permission mapping from Veza. The update ships with the Australia platform release. The Register (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-21, opens in new tab)

  6. 2026-04-20 · acquisition ServiceNow
    ServiceNow completes acquisition of Armis; Veza deal closed in March 2026

    ServiceNow announced on 2026-04-20 that it had completed its purchase of Armis, a cyber exposure management company, for about US$7.75 billion in cash funded from cash and debt. The release said the acquisition of Veza, an identity intelligence company, had closed in March 2026, and that signals from both feed its AI Control Tower. ServiceNow (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  7. 2026-03-02 · acquisition ServiceNow
    ServiceNow closes acquisition of identity security company Veza

    ServiceNow announced on 2025-12-02 that it would buy Veza, an identity security company founded in 2020 with about 230 staff and nearly 150 enterprise customers, for undisclosed terms; an update to the release says the deal closed on 2026-03-02. ServiceNow said Veza's Access Graph would be built into its AI Control Tower to govern what AI agents can reach.
